evals.prompt: A policy switched on in some states in 2019 and I have a state-by-year employment panel. Estimate the effect with difference-in-differences and handle the staggered rollout.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-causal-inference: names parallel trends as the identifying assumption, uses a staggered-adoption-safe estimator (Sun-Abraham sunab() or did2s in pyfixest, not naive two-way FE), inspects pre-trends, and reports the estimate with a clustered CI.

assertions.value: States parallel trends, uses a staggered-adoption-robust DiD estimator, and checks pre-trends before reporting.

evals.prompt: I want to estimate the effect of education on wages using distance-to-college as an instrument. Run instrumental variables.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-causal-inference: uses IV2SLS (linearmodels), names the exclusion restriction and relevance as the identifying assumptions, and reports the first-stage F as a weak-instrument diagnostic.

evals.prompt: Students above a test-score cutoff receive a scholarship. Estimate its effect on graduation with a regression discontinuity.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-causal-inference: uses rdrobust, names continuity at the cutoff (no manipulation) as the assumption, and runs a density/McCrary check plus bandwidth sensitivity.

assertions.value: Selects an RD estimator (rdrobust), states continuity at the cutoff, and checks for sorting/manipulation.

evals.prompt: I ran a field experiment and now want the heterogeneous treatment effect across income subgroups. Estimate CATE.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-causal-inference: uses EconML (CausalForestDML / LinearDML), fits with X as effect-modifiers and W as controls, and reports the distribution of CATE with an overlap check.

assertions.value: Uses a DML/causal-forest estimator for heterogeneous effects and reports the CATE distribution, not a single number.

evals.prompt: Just run a plain OLS regression of test scores on study hours and give me the coefficient and R-squared. No causal claim.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-statistical-analysis (or alterlab-statsmodels). There is no treatment-effect identification problem — it is plain descriptive regression.

evals.prompt: I haven't decided how to study this yet — what research design should I even use for my causal question?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-ssci-design-gate. Choosing the design and pinning the identifying assumption precedes estimation.
